summary: sextant-cli-darwin-arm64 ships Go binary with WebSocket-driven PTY backdoor and Anthropic key harvester
details: The package delivers a prebuilt Go binary at bin/sxt for darwin/arm64. The binary links a pseudo-terminal library (github.com/creack/pty), a WebSocket client (github.com/coder/websocket), and WebRTC (github.com/pion/webrtc/v4), and contains the hardcoded destinations wss://relay.sextant.top and https://relay.sextant.top/install. The combination is a network-to-shell dataflow: an author-controlled relay can drive a PTY on the installer's host, yielding full-host remote code execution. The binary additionally opens listeners on 0.0.0.0:7280, 0.0.0.0:7281, and 0.0.0.0:9000, exposing the shell surface on the local network. The same binary embeds an Anthropic API-key regex (sk-ant-[a-z0-9]+-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{40,}) alongside references to CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, claude.ai/install.sh, @google/gemini-cli, and https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models, indicating harvest of Claude Code and Gemini CLI credentials from the installer's environment for transmission over the relay. A call to http://ip-api.com/json/?fields=status,message,country,countryCode,city,timezone,isp,org,as,proxy,hosting,mobile,query fingerprints the installer's host and network (ISP, org, AS, proxy/hosting/mobile flags). The package.json license field points at https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control, so the author's own name for the binary is 'claude_control' despite the npm package presenting as a generic 'Sextant (sxt) binary for darwin/arm64'.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
